distractors.reason: We don't say 'much hungry'. 'Much' goes with uncountable nouns, such as much water, not with adjectives.
We don't say 'big hungry'. 'Big' is an adjective, so it cannot modify another adjective.
We don't say 'many hungry'. 'Many' goes with plural countable nouns, not with adjectives.

example_sentence: My dog is very hungry after its walk.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces traducen 'mucho' de forma literal y dicen 'much hungry' en lugar de 'very hungry'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the normal degree adverb before gradable adjectives such as hungry, big or happy. 'Much' is not used this way with adjectives.

related_collocations.example: The farm has a very big horse.
The cow is very tired after the day.

memory_tip: VERY = the normal word before adjectives (very big, very happy) | MUCH = before uncountable nouns (much water)
